[2026-10-25] c:6394558268 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK fab22ac42e350d4b4481515fe8ba2a319a744389

No test checks that `confTarget` still works under `-deprecatedrpc=confTarget`. The comment in `rpc_deprecated.py` asks that each deprecation tested there keep another functional test that still exercises it under the flag. `wallet_bumpfee.py` gains the flag, but its only `confTarget` call is the "should not both be set" error, so a change that broke `confTarget` behind the flag would still pass the tests. One `bumpfee` and one `psbtbumpfee` call with `{"confTarget": 6}` in that test would cover it.

The rest matched. Without the flag, both RPCs return -32 for `confTarget`, alone or next to `conf_target`, before the txid is looked up. With the flag, `confTarget` bumps and the conflict error is unchanged. `conf_target` works either way, positional or named. The help and `getopenrpcinfo` list only `conf_target`.

I measured this on regtest against a build of the head, with and without the flag, with calls sent through a client library I maintain. I can share the script and its output.
</new_statements>
